chapter: After Basie: Cafe Society to Los Angeles
title: Singing with Teddy Wilson and Art Tatum, and Andre Previn again
summary: Humes felt lucky to sing with great pianists. She calls Teddy Wilson the perfect accompanist, says Tatum played so much she wanted just to listen, and repeats the Previn story from the Contemporary sessions.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Well listen let's talk about those piano players a moment. I mean, that was really the thing to sing with guys like that, wasn't it?
Oh yeah, I thought I was so lucky.
Yeah, I mean for a singer that is lucky, isn't it?
But the biggest thing that ever happened to me was later whenI made my records for Contem-

porary, and I had Andre Previn.

Yeah. And you know he hadn't made any jazz records because he was always symphony. And he was terrific. And what part that made me feel so good was when I got ready to make my other session Mr. Koenig would call me and he said, "Helen, I want to ask something". I said, "what?" He said, "well, Andre Previn told me to ask you, could he be on the next session". I said, "are you kidding?" I was just so happy that he was on there and I wouldn't have had the nerve to ask him.
Isn't that nice.
Yes indeed.
How about that. When we get to that but let me identify those two sessions. That was wonderful. Well listen what about Teddy, of course, he was a wonderful accompanist.
Yeah. He's the greatest.
And he doesn't get in the way but he's there supporting you all the time.
Yeah.

And he doesn't suddenly konk out anywhere. But when you were singing with Art, that must have been something different because Art was such a piano player.
Yeah, I said wait a minute and give me a chance. He was just playing all that pretty stuff. When he does that I don't want to sing. I just want to listen.
Yeah. He was a nice man, wasn't he?
Oh yeah, and his wife and I, we used to visit each other.
That was very nice of her. Well, those must have been happy days at Cafe Society.
